payload.name: Preserve limiting qualifiers in extracted memories
payload.description: When extracting a memory candidate from a statement with quantifiers or qualifiers like 'a few', 'bits', 'some', 'partial', or 'almost', preserve them instead of generalizing to a whole or completed item.
content: During extraction, keep any quantifier or qualifier that materially limits or specifies the claim (e.g., 'a few bits', 'some pages', 'almost finished', 'partial draft'). Do not upgrade it to a full, complete, or whole version. If the source describes a portion or unfinished artifact, reflect that exact scope in the candidate content.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause was extraction normalizing 'a few bits for a screenplay' into 'a screenplay', dropping the quantifier 'bits' and inflating a partial work into a completed whole. This rule preserves limiting qualifiers and quantifiers during candidate extraction so that memories stay faithful to the source. It applies to any future statement containing modifiers such as 'a few', 'bits', 'some', 'partial', or 'almost' where dropping them would change the meaning, in any domain.

payload.name: Extract separate candidates for each distinct durable fact
payload.description: When a message states multiple distinct durable facts (e.g., how a skill was learned and who supported it), generate one memory candidate per fact instead of a single summary that omits some facts.
content: During candidate extraction, treat each distinct claim in a message as a separate durable fact (skills, preferences, events, relationships) and generate one candidate per claim; do not let a single summary drop any claim.

When a sentence contains multiple clauses with different predicates (e.g., 'I taught myself' and 'my dad was supportive'), create a separate candidate for each clause rather than only the clause that seems to fit an existing memory narrative.
If a fact is stated in an earlier message, extract it from that message; a later restatement is not a substitute for capturing the original occurrence.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that the extraction stage produced no candidate for the clearly stated fact 'learned to play on my own', and a later candidate captured only parental support while dropping the self-teaching claim. The reusable failure mechanism is treating a multi-fact message as one summary instead of several independent durable facts. This rule applies to any future utterance containing multiple facts about skills, preferences, events, or relationships, ensuring no durable claim is lost when another claim in the same message is captured.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: Use when a source message lists two or more distinct items (reasons, qualities, observations, preferences) and the construction extraction candidate must capture all of them.
content: During extraction, when the evidence explicitly enumerates multiple distinct items in a list (e.g., 'growth, improvement, and confidence'), include every listed item in the candidate content; do not replace the list with a single broader or synonymous term that drops any element.

If the candidate paraphrases but would omit one of the enumerated items, rephrase to name each item explicitly, even if the memory must be slightly longer, so that future questions about any single item remain answerable.

candidates.solves: When a source message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct items as a set (e.g., reasons, qualities, observations, preferences), the extraction candidate must preserve each enumerated element rather than paraphrase the whole list into a single broader term that omits any item. Future questions may test any one listed item, so losing a facet at extraction makes that fact unrecoverable later. This applies to any extraction candidate where the raw evidence contains a clear list of two or more discrete elements.

payload.name: Preserve enumerated facts and avoid unsupported objects
payload.description: When a user message explicitly lists multiple purposes, attributes, or uses of an entity, apply during candidate extraction and memory updates to capture every listed item without omitting any and without adding objects absent from the source.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source message explicitly enumerates multiple facts, purposes, or attributes of an entity, include all enumerated items in the candidate content; do not drop any listed item.
Do not introduce objects, tools, or unstated details into memory content unless they appear explicitly in the source message; paraphrase only what is actually said.
During UPDATE or MERGE, preserve every explicitly stated detail from the new source; if replacing a memory, carry the full set of stated facts forward rather than a partial subset.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is extraction that omitted two explicitly stated purposes and inserted an unmentioned whiteboard. The abstract failure mechanism is unfaithful paraphrase of enumerated source facts, leading to incomplete and hallucinated memory content. This skill applies to future construction tasks where a user lists multiple attributes, uses, or goals of an entity; it does not apply when the source is vague, when facts are implicit, or when a legitimate summary intentionally condenses repeated information.

payload.name: Preserve all distinct claims when extracting preferences
payload.description: Use during extraction when a single message states multiple distinct preferences, values, or evaluations about different activities, objects, or people; ensure each claim is captured before finalizing memory candidates.
content: When a source message contains multiple distinct preferences, values, or evaluations about different activities, objects, or people, generate one candidate per distinct claim, or one candidate that explicitly preserves every claim in wording.

Before finalizing extraction for a message, check that each distinct claim in the message appears in at least one candidate; do not drop a claim just because another claim in the same message seems more salient.
During batched ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, do not let a new candidate overwrite or merge away an existing memory claim that is still true; preserve all distinct true claims from the source.

candidates.solves: A single source message often lists several independent preferences or evaluations (e.g., time with one activity is valuable, time with another is relaxing). The diagnosed failure was that extraction kept only the more salient claim, so the stored memory missed a required fact. The skill ensures every distinct claim in a multi-claim utterance is preserved during extraction and not dropped during updates/merges. It applies to future messages containing parallel, contrastive, or enumerated statements about a person's preferences.

payload.name: Faithful extraction of enumerated claims
payload.description: When extracting memory candidates from a message that lists multiple distinct claims, strategies, or reasons, preserve each explicitly stated item and do not add details absent from the source.
content: During extraction, paraphrase the utterance completely: every explicitly stated claim (e.g., each strategy, reason, or preference the speaker lists) must appear in the candidate content; do not drop any item.

Do not add details not present in the source text, such as invented activities or examples. If a detail is not in the message, exclude it. Prefer omitting unstated embellishments over risking hallucination, but never omit stated claims.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction dropped Gina's explicitly stated 'reminding myself of my successes and progress' and added an unsupported 'dancing' detail, corrupting grounding. Abstract mechanism: candidate extraction can silently substitute or omit stated items when summarizing a multi-part utterance. The rule forces faithful, complete extraction of explicit claims without invented details. Applies to any future extraction where a speaker enumerates strategies, reasons, preferences, or facts.

payload.name: ExtractEachDurableFactSeparately
payload.description: When a single message contains more than one distinct durable fact (e.g., an action plus a background business/job/ownership state), create a separate extraction candidate for each fact during construction extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, treat each distinct durable fact in a message as its own candidate instead of merging them into the most salient action.

If a message mentions both an ongoing/enacted event (e.g., launching an ad campaign) and a durable status that explains it (e.g., starting/owning the store), emit one candidate for the event and one for the status fact.
Before finalizing a candidate list, check each message for background facts that future questions could compare across people; do not let a concrete action candidate absorb them.

candidates.solves: Extraction collapsed multiple distinct durable facts in one message into a single action-centric candidate, dropping a background fact (e.g., starting one's own business) that later cross-person comparisons need. This rule forces a separate candidate for each independently verifiable durable fact, preserving both foreground events and background states. Applies to any message combining an activity with an underlying status or ownership fact.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated reasons in memory extraction
payload.description: When a message lists several distinct reasons, traits, or attributes about a subject, apply this during extraction and CRUD to ensure every enumerated item is stored and none is dropped.
content: When a message explicitly lists multiple distinct reasons, traits, or attributes (e.g., 'because of A and B', 'it is X and Y'), include each enumerated item as a separate clause in the extraction candidate; do not collapse them into one general phrase.

During CRUD, when enriching an existing memory, compare the source message against the proposed content and add any enumerated reason/attribute that is missing, even if the memory already covers part of the list.
Before finalizing a candidate or update, re-check the source message to confirm that every explicitly stated fact is represented; if any is absent, expand the candidate content.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes drop one of several explicit reasons or attributes when a speaker lists multiple traits or justifications in one message, leaving memory incomplete for later questions. A rule that every enumerated fact must be carried into the candidate (and into enrichments during CRUD) directly addresses this mechanism and applies to any future message that lists multiple preferences, causes, features, or conditions.

payload.name: Preserve exact evaluative wording during extraction
payload.description: When extracting memory candidates from a message, if the source explicitly states an evaluative description, preserve that exact wording instead of replacing it with a synonym or paraphrase.
content: During extraction, when a source message contains an explicit evaluation or description, keep the speaker's exact adjective or phrase in the candidate content; do not substitute a near-synonym.
Before accepting a candidate that describes a subjective experience or quality, check the source message and confirm every distinctive evaluative word appears verbatim in the candidate.
Use generic summary language only when the source itself does not state a specific evaluative word; never normalize strong explicit wording into a weaker paraphrase.

candidates.solves: Caused by extraction paraphrasing an explicit evaluative adjective into a near-synonym, persisting in memory and failing exact-description recall. The reusable rule is to preserve exact evaluative wording when extracting memories from source statements. Applies to future extractions of explicit subjective descriptions; not applicable when source lacks exact wording or a neutral summary is intended.

payload.name: Preserve enumerated facts and do not skip unbacked candidates
payload.description: When extracting a candidate from a message that lists multiple distinct items, or when deciding whether to SKIP a candidate as duplicate, preserve every listed item and only SKIP if an existing memory covers it.
content: During extraction, when the source message enumerates multiple distinct items (e.g., 'chatted about X and Y', 'likes A, B, and C'), include each item explicitly in the candidate; do not replace the list with a broader paraphrase that omits any listed item.

During CRUD, before marking a candidate as SKIP because it is 'duplicate or already fully represented', check that there is an existing memory that actually covers the candidate's claims. If no such memory exists, ADD or MERGE the candidate instead of skipping it.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates that paraphrase a message containing multiple enumerated facts often drop one item, and the missing fact is later judged absent; candidates are also wrongly SKIPped as duplicates when no existing memory supports them. Applies to any construction session where one utterance lists distinct facts; does not require verbatim message reproduction, only preservation of every listed fact and evidence-backed duplicate checks.

payload.name: ExtractAllFactsFromMultiFactMessages
payload.description: When a user message states multiple distinct facts about the same subject and an extraction candidate is created, use separate candidates or full coverage so that no explicit fact is dropped.
content: During candidate extraction, a message containing multiple distinct facts must be covered by the candidate set as a whole; do not let one thematic candidate omit other explicit facts from the same message.
When facts in one message do not share a coherent theme, split them into separate ADD/UPDATE candidates instead of merging them under the dominant topic.
Before committing a batch, verify each source message against the candidates/updates it produced; any explicit fact missing from all of them must be added.

candidates.solves: An extraction candidate built around one dominant theme dropped an explicit fact from the same multi-fact message, and no later update restored it. The rule: treat each source message as fully covered by its candidate set—split distinct facts into separate candidates or ensure the combined set includes every explicit fact. Applies to any extraction batch where a message contributes several facts; not to choosing which facts are worth retaining.
